item.title: BA RUGBY NEWS I Late changes provide extra hurdle
item.description: Just as Round One of the Skipper Cup and Subrails Marama Championship approached, Ba’s preparations for their three matches with Suva were thrown into disarray when they heard the game had been brought forward by one day. “The late change, coming on Tuesday, caught us by surprise,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said.
item.content:encoded:
Just as Round One of the Skipper Cup and Subrails Marama Championship approached, Ba’s preparations for their three matches with Suva were thrown into disarray when they heard the game had been brought forward by one day.

“The late change, coming on Tuesday, caught us by surprise,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said.

“It seems there was a miscommunication somewhere along the line about the closure of HFC Bank Stadium this week.”

Not only did the new date mean rushed changes in travel and accommodation, but more importantly it altered team preparations.

“We told the players that these things were out of our control, so don’t let it affect you, just adjust and make do,” Kautoga said.

Some of the players in the NEWWORLD IGA Ba Women’s team were unable to take another day off work at such short notice, so they got left behind.

“They had already arranged to take leave on Friday, but couldn’t get the Thursday off as well when we were travelling around Viti Levu to Suva.”

“It’s a great pity for those players, but they can join us next week when we host Tailevu at 4R Stadium, Govind Park.”

As it happened, the young Ba Women, playing their first-ever match at this level against a side who have been champions multiple times, stood up to be counted.

Playing well-structured rugby, they raced to a 27-7 half-time lead after the opening score from Acelini Tuwai, a brace of tries to Balevuto winger Mereseini Saliucu, plus solo efforts from centre Reapi Savui and Veniasi Lumuka.

Former Fiji Soccer rep Sereana Naweni slotted in a penalty goal midway through the second half to give Ba a handy 30-12 lead, but Suva then showed their experience.

Taking advantage of two yellow cards against Ba within a minute, the large Suva forwards crashed through the Ba defence at regular intervals to narrow the gap.

Ba struggled to hold on, whilst butchering two near-certain tries of their own, and conceded twice in the closing two minutes to give Suva the win after the hooter.

“I’m so proud of these young players,” head coach Sitiveni Kuruvitu said.

“Everything has been stacked against us these past few weeks, but the girls played with such confidence and calmness.”

“To come to Suva, who have long-been a powerhouse in women’s rugby, and dominate some areas of play is a great achievement for our team.”

“We picked up two bonus points and can now look forward to the visit to Ba of Tailevu next week in the knowledge that we can compete at this level.”

The Fiji Pine U20’s suffered a similar heartbreak, conceding the winning try to their hosts after the hooter as Suva edged the game 24-21.

Suva had led 19-0 after half an hour, but the Penaia Cokomata-coached side found their rhythm and picked up three converted tries to lead 21-19 after 80 minutes.

Suva centre Joji Lutumailagi came strong when his side needed him and dived over for the winning score.

In the main Skipper Cup match, Vinod Patel Ba made a vast improvement over the last two encounters with Suva, but fell just short 26-28 when the last gasp conversion attempt sailed a metre wide.

Suva had jumped to an early 15-0 lead but Ba stayed close.

Tries in the final stages to replacement fullback Viliame Cama and wing Solo Druku brought Ba to the verge of their first-ever win over the Capitals, but Joseva Nokelevu couldn’t quite curl in his conversion.

So, Suva have started their campaigns with narrow wins in all three categories, but the efforts from the Ba teams will surely be recognised and built on.

Next Saturday, we can expect a bumper crowd for Tailevu’s visit to 4R Stadium, Govind Park. Tickets are $10 for adults, and $5 for children aged 5-11.

item.title: Eastern Zone Netball Rally ends on a high
item.description: The 2026 Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Rally concluded at Nasau Park in Levuka, with Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association vice president Joshua Qalo commending the standard of competition and the collective effort that delivered another successful championship. Qalo said the tournament produced exciting contests across all grades, particularly in the Under-15, U17 and U19 divisions.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Rally concluded at Nasau Park in Levuka, with Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association vice president Joshua Qalo commending the standard of competition and the collective effort that delivered another successful championship.

Qalo said the tournament produced exciting contests across all grades, particularly in the Under-15, U17 and U19 divisions.

“Leading up to the finals, it was an exciting performance by schools, particularly in the U19s, U15s and U17s, which were closely contested,” he said.

He also praised emerging schools that made their mark during the two-day competition.

“Wainibuka has shown they are going to be a team to watch at the Fiji Secondary Schools National Championships,” Qalo said.

He added that Vunimono High School (VHS) had also impressed throughout the tournament, proving they should not be overlooked heading into the national competition.

As the rally came to an end, Qalo thanked everyone who contributed behind the scenes.

“We’re thankful to the host schools, the Fiji Police Force, our umpires, scorers, stakeholders and everyone who contributed to making the Eastern Secondary Schools competition a success,” he said.

On the court, Adi Cakobau School (ACS) claimed the U14 title with a 19-9 victory over Lelean Memorial School (LMS). Wainibuka Secondary School (WBK) edged ACS 23-21 to win the U15 grade, while VHS defeated ACS 19-12 in the U17 final.

ACS bounced back to secure the U19 title after defeating Levuka Public School 35-21 before adding the Open Girls crown with a 15-9 win over WBK. VHS wrapped up the rally by edging Noco Secondary School 11-10 to claim the Open Men’s title.

Attention now turns to the Fiji Secondary Schools National Championships, where the Eastern Division’s top teams will look to build on their strong performances.

item.title: Ra, Macuata and Yasawa celebrate victories
item.description: “The supporters who came out in numbers gave us strength to keep pushing until the final whistle,” Ra captain Waisea Lawaibuka said after his side claimed a memorable 17-10 victory over Northland in the Vodafone Vanua Cup championship final yesterday. item.content:encoded:
“The supporters who came out in numbers gave us strength to keep pushing until the final whistle,” Ra captain Waisea Lawaibuka said after his side claimed a memorable 17-10 victory over Northland in the Vodafone Vanua Cup championship final yesterday. Ra capped off a remarkable campaign by lifting the title in front of a good crowd at Buckhurst Park, whose vocal support helped drive the team to victory.

The final was a physical contest, with both teams battling hard for possession and territory. Ra made the most of its opportunities to edge ahead before holding off a determined Northland outfit in the closing stages.

The captain credited the players for their commitment throughout the tournament and said the achievement was special for everyone involved with the team.

Lawaibuka extended his thanks to the supporters who attended in large numbers to back the team.

“Massive thank you to the supporters who turned up in numbers today. I was happy seeing the many people that came to cheer us on,” he said.

Meanwhile, Macuata and Yasawa celebrated title victories after producing impressive performances in their respective Vanua Cup finals yesterday.

Macuata claimed the under-20 title with a 30-10 win over Cakaudrove.

The final was closely contested early, with Macuata taking a 19-10 lead before capitalising on a Cakaudrove penalty to extend its advantage. A converted try later sealed the convincing victory.

Captain Sitiveni Raovu credited the players for their hard work and determination throughout the tournament.

“I would like to thank the boys for the hard work and effort they put in to secure this win,” he said.

Raovu acknowledged the challenges the team had faced, including receiving less support than the senior side, but said the players were grateful to have overcome those obstacles to lift the title.

In the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup final, Yasawa produced a dominant second-half display to defeat their opponents 43-15 after the teams were locked 10-10 at halftime.

Tight-head prop for the side Tulia Ragadi praised the team’s hard work and unity, saying their commitment had paid off.

“We are grateful to everyone who came out to support us. Their encouragement motivated us and played a big part in this victory,” she said.

item.title: Jasmine wins historic medal at Commonwealth Games
item.description: Trailblazing boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama hopes her historic Commonwealth Games bronze medal will inspire more women and girls across Fiji to step into the boxing ring. The 21-year-old made history as the first Fijian woman to represent the country in international boxing and added another milestone to her career by securing a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow early this morning Fij
item.content:encoded:
Trailblazing boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama hopes her historic Commonwealth Games bronze medal will inspire more women and girls across Fiji to step into the boxing ring.

The 21-year-old made history as the first Fijian woman to represent the country in international boxing and added another milestone to her career by securing a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow early this morning Fiji time.

Although she was defeated by Northern Ireland’s reigning featherweight champion Michaela Walsh in the semi-finals, Daunakamakama’s run to the last four guaranteed her a place on the podium and cemented her place in Fiji’s sporting history.

Speaking after the unanimous points loss, an emotional Daunakamakama described the achievement as both rewarding and heartbreaking.

“I’m very proud of myself for entering this competition with only a little over 20 bouts.

“On paper, I may be quite inexperienced, but I am proud that my mana carried me through this far into this competition.”

Her bronze medal continues Fiji’s proud boxing tradition at the Commonwealth Games. Fine Sani claimed gold in the light heavyweight division at the 1982 Brisbane Games, while Winston Hill won bronze in the welterweight division at the 2018 Gold Coast Games.

Daunakamakama fought back tears after her final bout and was embraced by coach Cameron Todd in an emotional moment away from the crowd.

Despite taking up boxing just three years ago, she defeated Ghana’s Adelaide Djabatey and Sri Lanka’s Keshani Hansika on her way to the semi-finals, ensuring Fiji would once again feature among the medal winners.

She said the encouragement she received from fellow Pacific athletes throughout the Games strengthened her resolve.

“Before walking into this competition, I knew I carried a lot of responsibility as one of the most experienced female boxers in Fiji,” she said.

“It’s a great reminder of how much pride and unity we carry as Pacific Islanders.

“No matter how far we are from home, we still unite as one and continue to push ourselves in this sport.”

Daunakamakama hopes her breakthrough achievement will encourage more Fijian women to pursue boxing and prove that they too can succeed on the international stage.

“I hope that when I get home, this will inspire the next generation,” she said.

item.title: Dad: Bring it home
item.description: Those were the words of encouragement from Fiji Amateur Boxing Association president Panapasa Daunakamakama to his daughter Jasmine after she secured a place in the semi-finals of the women’s 57kg division at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in Scotland. Jasmine kept Fiji’s medal hopes alive after defeating Sri Lanka’s Keshani Hansika by a 4-1 split points decision in the quarter-finals, guaran
item.content:encoded:
Those were the words of encouragement from Fiji Amateur Boxing Association president Panapasa Daunakamakama to his daughter Jasmine after she secured a place in the semi-finals of the women’s 57kg division at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in Scotland.

Jasmine kept Fiji’s medal hopes alive after defeating Sri Lanka’s Keshani Hansika by a 4-1 split points decision in the quarter-finals, guaranteeing herself at least a bronze medal and moving within one win of the gold medal bout.

Speaking from his office in Wailada, Lami yesterday, Panapasa said the achievement belonged to everyone who had supported Jasmine throughout her journey.

“The glory goes back to God, and everyone involved in the journey. From the coaches to the technical team, to the family support and the support from all coaches and judges, this is for everyone,” he said.

Reflecting on Jasmine’s preparation before the Games, Panapasa said he believed she was ready for the challenge.

“Before she went into the Commonwealth Games, I knew she had ticked all the boxes which she hadn’t going into previous professional competitions.”

The proud father said he reminded Jasmine of the biblical story of David and Goliath after her quarter-final victory.

“It was a proud moment for everyone involved and when I spoke to her after the quarter final I reminded her of the David and Goliath story from the bible.

“I know it is going to get tough from here but my message to her was to ‘Bring it home.”

Jasmine will step back into the ring at 6am tomorrow, with victory in the semi-final earning her a place in the gold medal bout as she continues her pursuit of Commonwealth Games glory.

item.title: Jasmine inspires a new generation
item.description: JASMINE Daunakamakama has already guaranteed herself a place in Fiji’s sporting history. Now, professional boxer Winston Hill believes her Commonwealth Games breakthrough could transform women’s boxing in the country for years to come.
item.content:encoded:
JASMINE Daunakamakama has already guaranteed herself a place in Fiji’s sporting history.

Now, professional boxer Winston Hill believes her Commonwealth Games breakthrough could transform women’s boxing in the country for years to come.

The former Commonwealth Games bronze medallist says Daunakamakama’s march into the women’s 57kg semi-finals in Glasgow is a milestone that extends far beyond the ring.

“There is just so much pride around not just Jasmine but the whole Fijian team,” Hill said.

“History has been made with Jasmine. She is the first Fijian female boxer to reach this stage at the Commonwealth Games, and she has already secured a bronze medal.”

Daunakamakama now faces the toughest test of her career against reigning 2022 Commonwealth Games gold medalist Northern Ireland’s Michaela Walsh for a place in the gold medal bout.

Hill knows exactly what it takes to compete on boxing’s biggest amateur stage. He claimed bronze at the 2018 Commonwealth Games on the Gold Coast and said the occasion demands as much mental strength as physical preparation.

“When I competed in the amateurs, it was my closest moment with God,” he said.

“I went through a very strong spiritual journey during training and out on the field of play. I’m sure with her people behind her, her country and her faith, she will make Fiji proud no matter what happens.”

Hill said there was no need for Daunakamakama to change her approach despite the magnitude of the contest.

“This is her first international competition, and she has already reached the semi-finals. That is a huge milestone. She should take everything in, enjoy the experience and keep building from here.”

“The national coach is doing a fantastic job preparing both the men and Jasmine. She just needs to give it her best and know the whole country is proud of her.”

A victory over Walsh would secure at least a silver medal and put Daunakamakama within one win of Commonwealth Games gold.

For Hill, that achievement would deserve recognition far beyond the boxing community.

“If she beats Michaela Walsh, she goes into the gold or silver fight. That would be amazing,” he said.

“She deserves to come back to Fiji and be recognised. Businesses and corporate sponsors should get behind her and help create a solid pathway for her future.

“It is not just about Jasmine. It is about inspiring more young women to take up boxing.”

The Women’s 57 kg division is one of the most fiercely competitive and star-studded brackets in the 2026 Glasgow meet with nine countries represented in the division.

While it has a modest field size, the concentration of elite, world-class talent makes it a major highlight of the Games.

Away from boxing, Daunakamakama has also pursued her passion for music.

She was part of the V5 band that reached the top 10 of the national Domo Vou Talei songwriting competition with their original song Mango Tree, highlighting the talent and determination that have now carried her onto the Commonwealth Games podium.

Hill believes Daunakamakama’s historic campaign has shown that Fijian women can compete with the world’s best and could become the spark that lifts women’s boxing to new heights in Fiji.

Jasmine Daunakamakama’s semifinal bout is set for tomorrow morning, Saturday August 1, 2026, at 6am.

item.title: Suva netters rally on
item.description: SUVA Sangam College open grade team is determined to build on its Suva Zone Two success when it competes at the Central Rally this week. Open grade captain Fipe Sorocala, a year thirteen student, said the team had put in the hard work during the lead-up to the tournament and was confident of taking on the top schools.
item.content:encoded:
SUVA Sangam College open grade team is determined to build on its Suva Zone Two success when it competes at the Central Rally this week.

Open grade captain Fipe Sorocala, a year thirteen student, said the team had put in the hard work during the lead-up to the tournament and was confident of taking on the top schools.

“We have been preparing throughout the week,” Sorocala said.

The team heads into the competition after claiming the Suva Zone Two title, a result that has boosted the players’ confidence ahead of the Central Rally.

Fipe acknowledged that the standard of competition would be much higher but said the players were looking forward to the challenge.

“We are excited, and we are prepared to face the bigger schools,” she said.

Sorocala said the team had focused on building strong combinations and improving communication during training, which had helped strengthen the players’ understanding of one another.

“We have prepared ourselves well over the past few days, and everyone knows their role within the team.

We are ready to move forward,” she said.

Sorocala believes the team’s preparation and unity will be key as Suva Sangam aims to continue its winning form and challenge for top honours at the Central Rally.

item.title: Singh wants strong finish
item.description: NAVUA will look to turn its recent lessons into a stronger performance when it meets a determined Tailevu Naitasiri side in the Extra Premier League Round 16 clash on Sunday. Coach Rodicks Singh expects a demanding contest, with Tailevu Naitasiri fighting to keep its place in the competition and likely to bring plenty of intensity to the match.
item.content:encoded:
NAVUA will look to turn its recent lessons into a stronger performance when it meets a determined Tailevu Naitasiri side in the Extra Premier League Round 16 clash on Sunday.

Coach Rodicks Singh expects a demanding contest, with Tailevu Naitasiri fighting to keep its place in the competition and likely to bring plenty of intensity to the match.

“The preparations and expectations are both going to need to be very intense because we know we’re playing a side that is fighting for survival,” Singh said.

For Navua, the match presents an opportunity to build on its strengths while addressing areas that have prevented the team from producing consistent performances.

Singh believes his players have shown what they are capable of but wants them to find greater consistency from one match to the next.

“We’re not consistent. We win one week; we have come down with two losses back-to-back. We are not consistent in the way we want to play,” he said.

The coach said the focus now is on turning those lessons into improvement and ensuring the team maintains its intensity throughout the match.

Finishing strongly is another area Navua is working to improve.

“Our finishing part is still a very worrying factor. Our area of concern is how we finish the game,” Singh said.

He said the team has allowed its intensity to drop during the final 15 minutes of recent matches, giving opponents opportunities to take advantage.

“If you look at the past two games, it is the last part of the game that is really hurting us,” he said.
